newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog keen to sort out pension mis-selling.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog keen to sort out pension mis-selling.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) repeated its commitment to resolving the issue of pension mis-selling on Thursday as the financial markets regulator outlined its plans for the year.
Investors who were mis-sold pensions and suffered loss were entititled to compensation, the SIB said in a statement, and it was determined they should get it.
It described progress on the issue as "unacceptably slow" and said firms dragging their feet could expect a "robust regulatory response".

Earlier this week the Personal Investment Authority (PIA), which regulates the sale of pensions and other investments to the public, announced the setting up of a new enforcement unit to speed up the inquiry -- begun in 1994 -- into pensions mis-selling.
Another area likely to come under increasing scrutiny by the SIB is developing technology, such as the internet, and the implications it poses for regulation and investor protection.
"We need to to respond to new developments in technology... so as to ensure that their potential can be realised without harm to investors," said SIB chairman Sir Andrew Large.
The SIB also said it planned to launch a review of clearing and settlement services, trading services and information and rating services.

After a series of high-profile problems in recent years, often sharing the common thread of management failure, the SIB said its overall aim was to find the best way of encouraging firms to live up to their responsibilities, said the SIB. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
